title: In 1947, a Ship Exploded and Threw a 2-Ton Anchor 1.5 Miles

scenes.text: A ship's two-ton anchor once flew a mile and a half.
The ship was the Grandcamp, loaded with about 2,300 tons of fertilizer in Texas City.
The blast sent up a fifteen-foot wave and knocked two small planes out of the sky.
It broke windows in Galveston, ten miles away.
It killed nearly 600 people, and it is the deadliest industrial disaster in American history.
The anchor landed in a ten-foot crater. It happened in 1947.

description:
In 1947 the ship Grandcamp exploded in Texas City, Texas, and threw its two-ton anchor about a mile and a half.
The blast carried about 2,300 tons of ammonium nitrate, knocked planes out of the sky and killed nearly 600 people.
Had you heard of the Texas City disaster?

first_comment: The blast was recorded on a seismograph in Denver, about a thousand miles away. Had you heard of this one?
